items.prompt: A photorealistic photograph of Lisbon seen from the river Tagus, late afternoon golden light, soft haze, gentle ripples and reflections on calm water, shot on a 35mm lens. Keep the composition of the reference image exactly: the river Tagus fills the lower half, the horizon sits at mid-height, the hill of Lisbon rises in the centre distance, and a stone quay with three barrels and a bollard sits in the lower right corner. The left two-thirds of the water must be open and empty: no ships, boats or people there. No people in the foreground. No text, no frame, no border. Historically accurate Lisbon in 1451: the Castle of São Jorge crowning the hill with medieval stone walls and square towers; the Alfama quarter below it, whitewashed houses with terracotta roofs stacked down the slope; the twin-towered Romanesque cathedral (Sé) among them; a low medieval stone wall along the riverfront. No Belém Tower, no modern buildings, no bridges, no grand waterfront square.
